title: Non-Desarguesian Planes: The Moulton Plane Counterexample
description: Formalizes the Moulton plane (1902) — a non-Desarguesian affine plane over ℝ — and provides an explicit rational-coordinate counterexample showing that Desargues's theorem fails. Two triangles are in perspective from a point yet their corresponding-side intersections are not Moulton-collinear.

overview.historicalContext: Desargues's theorem was proved in 1639 and holds in all projective spaces of dimension ≥ 3. For projective planes (2-dimensional), however, the theorem is not a consequence of the projective plane axioms alone. In 1902, Forest Ray Moulton constructed the first simple counterexample: a modified affine plane over ℝ where lines with positive slope are 'bent' at the y-axis (the right half-plane portion has slope halved). This plane satisfies all affine plane axioms but fails Desargues. It established that Desargues's theorem characterises precisely the planes that can be coordinatised by a skew field (division ring).
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Question**: Can we formalize non-Desarguesian projective planes in Lean to demonstrate when Desargues's theorem fails?

**Answer**: YES. The Moulton affine plane, formalized here, is a non-Desarguesian affine plane with an explicit rational-coordinate counterexample.
overview.text:
The Moulton plane uses ordinary Cartesian points ℝ × ℝ but a modified line structure. A 'Moulton line' with left-slope m and y-intercept b follows y = mx + b for x ≤ 0, but for m > 0 the right half-plane portion bends to slope m/2: y = (m/2)x + b for x > 0. Negative-slope and vertical lines are unchanged.

The counterexample uses center O = (0,0) and triangles A = (-2,3), B = (3,1), C = (0,-1) and A' = (-4,6), B' = (9,3), C' = (0,-4). Lines OAA' (slope -3/2), OBB' (slope 2/3, bent), and OCC' (vertical x=0) confirm perspectivity from O. The intersections P = AB ∩ A'B' = (-17,9), Q = BC ∩ B'C' = (27,17), R = CA ∩ C'A' = (-6,11) are Euclidean-collinear (classical Desargues holds in ℝ²), but the Moulton line through P and R (left slope 2/11, right slope 1/11) reaches y = 160/11 ≈ 14.5 at x = 27 — not 17 = Q.y. So P, Q, R are NOT Moulton-collinear.
overview.proofStrategy:
1. **Definition**: `onMoultonLine m b P` is a piecewise predicate — ordinary line for m ≤ 0, bent line (slope m left, m/2 right) for m > 0. `MoultonCollinear` quantifies over all Moulton lines.
2. **Perspectivity**: Three direct incidence checks (each by norm_num) establish OAA', OBB', OCC' Moulton-collinear.
3. **Non-collinearity**: Proof by contradiction. Case m ≤ 0: slope PQ = 2/11 > 0, immediate linarith. Case m > 0: P and R equations determine m = 16/61 and b = 821/61 uniquely; plugging into R's equation gives 725/61 ≠ 671/61, contradiction by linarith.
keyInsights: The bending rule (slope halved on right half-plane) is the minimal perturbation that breaks Desargues while preserving the affine plane axioms

All side-intersection computations use only negative-slope or same-half-plane Moulton lines, so P, Q, R are computed by ordinary linear algebra — the bending is only visible when testing collinearity of P, Q, R
The non-collinearity proof splits cleanly into two linarith calls: one for m ≤ 0 and one for m > 0, each deriving a numeric contradiction from the three point equations
P, Q, R ARE Euclidean-collinear (slope 2/11), confirming classical Desargues holds in ℝ² — only the Moulton plane's bent lines reveal the failure

The algebraic connection: Desargues iff coordinatizable by a division ring (Wedderburn 1905 / Hilbert 1901). The Moulton plane's violation of Desargues reflects a non-associativity in the ternary ring that arises from the piecewise multiplication by 1/2 at the y-axis

sections.title: Part I: Moulton Line Structure
sections.summary: Defines onMoultonLine m b P (piecewise: ordinary for m≤0, bent for m>0 at x=0 boundary), MoultonCollinear (vertical or exists m,b), and six helper lemmas as constructors/destructors for the piecewise predicate.
sections.mathContext: Moulton line: $y = mx+b$ for $x \leq 0$ and $y = \frac{m}{2}x+b$ for $x > 0$ (when $m > 0$). The boundary $x=0$ is consistent: both halves give $y = b$. Helper lemmas avoid repeated case splits.

sections.title: Part II: Counterexample Points
sections.mathContext: Rational coordinates: all 10 points have integer or half-integer coordinates in $\mathbb{Q} \subset \mathbb{R}$, enabling exact arithmetic by norm_num.

sections.title: Part III: Perspectivity from O
sections.summary: collinear_OAA' (slope -3/2, ordinary), collinear_OBB' (left-slope 2/3, right-slope 1/3, bent), collinear_OCC' (vertical). Establishes that ABC and A'B'C' are in Moulton perspective from O=(0,0).
sections.mathContext: Three qualitatively distinct Moulton collinearities: negative slope (ordinary), positive slope with a right-half-plane point (bent), vertical. Each requires different onML_* lemmas.

sections.title: Part IV: Intersection Points
sections.summary: 14 incidence lemmas placing P, Q, R on the six pairs of corresponding sides. P and R lie on negative-slope ordinary Moulton lines; Q lies on positive-slope lines at x>0 (right half).

sections.title: Part V: Desargues Fails
sections.summary: desargues_fails: ¬ MoultonCollinear P Q R by contradiction. Vertical case: P.1≠Q.1. m≤0 case: linarith from slope of PQ = 2/11 > 0. m>0 case: linear_combination gives 11m=2 and 61m=16, contradicted by linarith.
sections.mathContext: $m \leq 0$: slope $PQ = 8/44 = 2/11 > 0$, contradicts $m \leq 0$. $m > 0$: P and R on left ($x \leq 0$), Q on right ($x > 0$) — system $\{9=-17m+b,\; 17=27m/2+b,\; 11=-6m+b\}$ gives $11m=2$ and $61m=16$; contradiction $122 = 176$.

sections.title: Part VI: Full Counterexample Certificate
sections.summary: moulton_counterexample packages all 22 conjuncts (3 perspectivity + 18 incidence + 1 non-collinearity) as a single anonymous constructor. No tactics needed — pure term-mode proof.
sections.mathContext: Formal certificate: $\forall$ claims are machine-verified by norm_num + ring + linarith. The statement is an explicit conjunction covering all incidence data of the Desargues counterexample.

conclusion.summary: The Moulton plane provides a fully formalized, axiom-free counterexample to Desargues's theorem in an affine plane over ℝ. The main theorem `desargues_fails` is proved by a two-case linarith argument requiring only rational arithmetic. The full certificate `moulton_counterexample` packages 22 machine-verified incidence and non-incidence conditions.
conclusion.implications: Combined with desargues-theorem-oq-01 (which proves Desargues over any commutative ring using homogeneous coordinates), this gives a complete picture: Desargues holds in coordinate planes over fields/division rings and fails in planes with weaker coordinatization. The formalization uses only Mathlib's real arithmetic and tactic library — no topology, no continuity, no algebraic geometry. The Lean proof demonstrates that the entire classical independence argument can be mechanized with 260 lines and no axioms beyond Lean's logical foundation.
openQuestions: Can the Moulton plane be extended to a projective plane (adding a line at infinity) and the failure of Desargues proved in the projective completion?
Can the smallest finite non-Desarguesian projective plane (order 9, the Hall plane) be formalized in Lean using nearfield coordinatization?
Can the algebraic equivalence (Desargues ↔ coordinatizable by a division ring) be formalized in Lean, completing the characterization theorem?
